title: Kitebird and Tulsiwala Books partnership call

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: Hello Sarah, hello Deepak. Thanks for joining from your side, Hina is with me as well.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Hi Arvind, hi Hina. Good to finally put faces to the emails.

segments.speaker: Deepak Yadav
segments.text: Hello everyone.

segments.speaker: Hina Mirza
segments.text: Hi. I've read your catalogue, the science series would fit our app very well.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: Let me set the context. Kitebird Learning wants to put Tulsiwala Books' middle school titles inside our reading app.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: And we want to understand how many students would actually read them, before we commit our whole catalogue.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: Which is why we suggested a pilot first.

segments.speaker: Deepak Yadav
segments.text: How big a pilot are you thinking?

segments.speaker: Hina Mirza
segments.text: Two hundred student licences across three of our partner schools, for three months.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Three months is short. Reading habits take time to show.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: True, but if it goes well we expand in the new academic year anyway.

segments.speaker: Deepak Yadav
segments.text: From the content side, three months is easier, we only need to convert twelve titles.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Okay. Let's go with a three-month pilot of 200 licences.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: Great, that's settled then.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Now the money. How do we split revenue from the paid licences?

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: We proposed sixty percent to you, forty to us, since we carry the platform cost.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Our authors expect at least seventy percent, that's what print gives them.

segments.speaker: Hina Mirza
segments.text: Print has no app hosting or support costs.

segments.speaker: Deepak Yadav
segments.text: But print has paper and distribution. I'd say it evens out.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: Let me be practical. Seventy-thirty in your favour for the pilot, and we review it for the full rollout.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Seventy-thirty for the pilot works for us.

segments.speaker: Hina Mirza
segments.text: So revenue share is seventy percent to Tulsiwala, thirty to Kitebird, during the pilot.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Yes. I'll put this in a draft agreement.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: When could we see the draft?

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Our lawyer is quick. I'll send the draft agreement next Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: Next Tuesday is good. Just so you know, our office is closed from 24 December to 1 January, so replies may be slow then.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Same for us, more or less. We'll keep it moving before that.

segments.speaker: Hina Mirza
segments.text: Content format. Our app needs EPUB with proper chapter markers.

segments.speaker: Deepak Yadav
segments.text: We have EPUB for most titles. The illustrated ones need work.

segments.speaker: Hina Mirza
segments.text: Could you share a few sample files so our tech team can test the import?

segments.speaker: Deepak Yadav
segments.text: I'll share sample EPUB files for three titles by 8 January, after the holidays.

segments.speaker: Hina Mirza
segments.text: That's fine, the pilot schools only start in February.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: One thing our marketing team keeps asking for is a co-branded print edition. Both logos on the cover.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: That's a big step, it changes your print contracts and our brand rules.

segments.speaker: Hina Mirza
segments.text: I'd rather not mix that into the pilot. Let's see the numbers first.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Fair enough, we'll leave the co-branded edition for later.

segments.speaker: Deepak Yadav
segments.text: What about student data? Schools ask a lot about that.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: The data stays on our servers in India, and you get only aggregated reading numbers.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Our legal people will want that clause written very carefully.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: Then the legal teams on both sides need to review the data clause in two weeks, before anything is signed.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Two weeks is realistic, as long as the draft goes out first.

segments.speaker: Deepak Yadav
segments.text: Do we need a launch event at the schools?

segments.speaker: Hina Mirza
segments.text: A short session for teachers would be enough. Students learn the app in minutes.

segments.speaker: Deepak Yadav
segments.text: I can bring two of our authors for a reading at one school, if that helps.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: That would be lovely, let's plan it once the pilot starts.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: How will we measure success?

segments.speaker: Hina Mirza
segments.text: Weekly active readers and chapters completed. We'll share a dashboard view every month.

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: Monthly is good. My director will ask for those numbers.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: Anything else from your side?

segments.speaker: Sarah Lobo
segments.text: No, this was productive. Talk soon.

segments.speaker: Arvind Chatterjee
segments.text: Thank you, everyone. Have a good evening.

decisions.fact: A three-month pilot with 200 student licences goes ahead.
Pilot revenue is split 70% to the publisher and 30% to the app.

action_items.fact: Deepak shares sample EPUB files for three titles.
Both companies' legal teams review the student data clause; no person named.

distractors.fact: A co-branded print edition was suggested and left for later.
24 December to 1 January is Kitebird's office closure, not the agreement's due date.
